sentences.text:
Apsrtc vs Eedi Santhi on 17 October, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Justice Dr. V.R.K.Krupa Sagar
 Macma No.399 of 2022
Judgment:

In this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, APSRTC impugns the order dated 22.12.2021 of learned Chairman, Motor Vehicle Claims Tribunal - Cum - Principal District Judge,
Rajamahendravaram in M.V.O.P.No.481 of 2018.

entities.text:
Motor Vehicle Claims Tribunal - Cum - Principal District Judge,
Rajamahendravaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Respondent No.6 is the driver of the offending APSRTC bus and in this appeal, the appellant states that he is not a necessary party.
Respondent Nos.1 to 5 are the claimants.
Respondent Nos. 2 to 4 are minor children represented by their natural guardian/1st respondent.
3. Sri Vinod Kumar Tarlada, learned Standing Counsel for APSRTC and Sri N.Siva Reddy, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 5/claimants submitted arguments.
4. The facts leading to the present appeal are required to be noticed:
Sri E. Arjunudu aged 26 years was a vegetable vendor earning about Rs.10,000/- per month.
On 23.07.2018, he along with his wife were going on motor cycle bearing No.AP 05 CT 6115.
His relations were following them on another motor cycle.

Dr. VRKS, J On N.H.16 road near Joduthumulu of Dharmavaram Village of Prathipadu Mandal, East Godavari District at about 10:00 a.m., while the motor cycles were going on, APSRTC Garuda Volvo RTC bus bearing No.AP16Z 0483 came rashly or negligently and dashed the motor cycle and as a consequence Sri E.Arjunudu fell down from the bike and the rear wheels of the bus ran over his head leading to his death on the spot.

As against the offending bus driver, a case was registered by police and that was investigated into and charge sheet was laid before learned Magistrate attributing negligence on part of the driver of the APSRTC bus.
The wife and the minor children and the mother of the deceased moved their claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/-.

The driver as well as employer/APSRTC filed their counters denying the version narrated in the claim petition and further stated that there was no negligence on part of the driver and the deceased had no driving license and the deceased was driving the motorcycle without care and caution and influencing the police a false case was filed against the driver of the bus and they sought dismissal of the claim.
Dr. VRKS, J 5.
Learned claims tribunal framed the following issues for its consideration.

Apsrtc vs Eedi Santhi on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99470790/
1 Issues: -
1.

Whether the deceased Eedi Arjunudu, S/o.Late Malayya died in a motor accident on 23.07.2018 on N.H.16 road near Jodu Thumulu, outskirts of Dharmavaram Village, Prathipadu Mandal due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the 1st respondent/driver of APSRTC Garuda Volva bus bearing No. AP 16 Z 0483?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation, if so, to what amount and from which of the respondents?

3. To what relief?
6.
At the trial, wife of deceased testified as PW.1 and got marked Exs.A1 to A5.
The driver of the offending bus testified as RW.1 and no documents were adduced in evidence.

7. After considering the entire evidence on record and on considering the arguments advanced on both sides, the learned claims tribunal held that PW.1 was eyewitness and within hours after the incident Ex.A1/FIR was registered wherein the Dr. VRKS, J registration number of the offending bus was mentioned.

It observed that as per the evidence of PW.1 and also as per the investigative outcome of the state police contained in Ex.A4/charge sheet, the accident occurred was because of rash or negligent driving on part of the driver of the offending APSRTC bus.
The relationship of the claimants with the deceased was found undisputed.
The occupation of the deceased was vegetable vending and his age was found to be anywhere between 26 to 30 years by the time of accident.
His income was fixed at Rs.7,000/- and multiplier "17" was applied.
It calculated the compensation accordingly.
Finally, it awarded Rs.10,71,000/- towards loss of dependency.
Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
Rs. 40,000/- towards loss of consortium were also awarded.
Thus, a total compensation of Rs.11,41,000/- was awarded.
It granted 6% interest per annum from the time of petition till the time of realization.
The driver and employer/APSRTC were held jointly and severally liable and the employer/APSRTC was directed to satisfy the award by depositing the amounts within one month.

It apportioned the amount to the claimants and Dr.
VRKS, J took care of keeping the share of amount of minors in fixed deposits till they attain majority for appropriate disbursal.
8. It is that award which is challenged by the APSRTC in this appeal.

In the memorandum of grounds of appeal, it is stated that deceased had no driving license and driving a motor bike without a license was a crime and by his driving, he contributed to the accident and the APSRTC bus was not involved in this incident and the tribunal erroneously recorded its findings ignoring these contentions.
That the notional income of Rs.7,000/- per month assessed by the claims tribunal is incorrect and it should have been Rs.3,000/- per month.

During arguments Sri Vinod Kumar Tarlada, learned Standing Counsel for APSRTC forcefully contended that there was no evidence indicating income of the deceased and in such circumstances claims tribunal fixing the notional income of Rs.7,000/- is incorrect.

Apsrtc vs Eedi Santhi on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99470790/
2 9.

As against this, learned counsel for respondents submits that the entire evidence available on record was appreciated by the claims tribunal and from the evidence appropriate conclusions were arrived at and for a man engaged in business Dr. VRKS, J of sale of vegetables fixing the notional income at Rs.7,000/- disagreeing with the claim of Rs.10,000/- per month cannot be challenged in this appeal.
Learned counsel submits that there is no warrant for interference.
10. At the bar Minu Rout V. Satya Pradyumna Mohapatra1 is cited.

entities.text: Minu Rout V. Satya Pradyumna Mohapatra1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case, the collision was between a car and a truck.
Compensation was claimed against owner, driver and insurer of the truck.
Evidence produced before the tribunal indicated negligence on part of the driver of the truck and that was the cause of accident.
However, Courts below arrived at findings about contributory negligence.

On assessment of all the facts and principles of law, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India set aside that finding and held that as per the evidence made available, there was no contributory negligence and exclusive liability was with driver, owner and insurer of the truck.
That was a case where the deceased was found to be a driver by occupation and his proclaimed income was Rs.5,000/- per month.
Courts below acted upon that.

However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India found fault with that and held that the (2013) 10 SCC 695 Dr. VRKS, J income of the deceased should have been considered at Rs.6,000/- per month and further held that 30% future prospects were to be added as the deceased was aged 35 years and their Lordships made necessary calculations and revised the compensation.

11. Point that falls for consideration is: -
"Whether the impugned award is incorrect for granting excess compensation as contended by the appellant?"
POINT:-
Undisputed facts are that Sri E.Arjunudu while driving the motor cycle suffered an automobile accident on 23.07.2018 at about 10.00 a.m., and sustained serious injuries and died on the spot.
Before the claims tribunal as well as here, the contention raised on behalf of APSRTC is that APSRTC bus bearing No.AP16 Z 0483 was not involved in this incident but it was falsely implicated.
The driver of the APSRTC bus contended before the claims tribunal was that by the time of alleged accident his bus already reached a different place at Gandepalli.
The evidence on record was that of the eyewitness/PW.1 who was the very wife of the deceased.
She had no enmity as against Dr. VRKS, J APSRTC bus driver since she had no other acquaintance with him earlier to this incident.
By 12.30 p.m., FIR was registered and it contained the registration number of the APSRTC bus.
6th respondent herein was the driver of the said bus at the material point of time is not in dispute.
There was no evidence on record to indicate that by the time of accident, the bus was not at the spot of accident but it was at a different place at Gandepalli.
The investigation of police also revealed involvement of this very bus in this incident.

With such evidence on record claims tribunal rightly concluded that APSRTC bus bearing registration No.AP 16 Z 0483 was driven by Sri Angada Veeranjaneyulu/6th respondent herein and was Apsrtc vs Eedi Santhi on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99470790/
3 involved in this accident.
The contention of the APSRTC is that deceased had no driving license to drive motorcycle and he was at fault and contributed for the accident.
There is no merit in this contention.
The investigative outcome of police as contained in Ex.A4/charge sheet does not support this contention.
The evidence of PW.1 specifically condemned this version.
That the appellant failed to produce any evidence to indicate that the deceased had no driving license is apparent from the record.
Even if the deceased did not have driving license that by itself cannot be called as a Dr. VRKS, J cause for accident.
There must be evidence to indicate that he was unable to drive properly and his inability to drive resulted in the accident.
Satisfying that standard there was no evidence either from PW.1 or from other sources.
Therefore, this contention of appellant has no basis and is thus negatived.
12. The prime contention raised is about tribunal fixing monthly income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/-.
Having analysed the material on record, this court finds no merit in this contention for the following reasons.
Undisputed evidence and the findings of the tribunal which have not fallen for challenge here are - age of the deceased was between 26 to 30 years and he was doing his business in vegetables.
Income of the deceased was spoken to by his wife/PW.1 as Rs.10,000/- per month.
Except questioning the correctness of income, neither the counters nor the evidence led by driver of the APSRTC indicate anything contrary.
In other words, the driver and APSRTC did not plead as to what was the occupation of the deceased and how much was his income.
Thus, they had no positive case.
In such circumstances, the evidence that was brought before the tribunal had to be considered.
A vendor of vegetables in villages is quite unlikely to Dr. VRKS, J pass receipts for sales and maintain books of accounts.
Taking pragmatic approach, his income had to be considered.
He was a self-employed businessman.
The incident occurred in the year 2018.
He and his relations were going on motor bikes at the relevant time which fact indicated his financial capacity to own and use motor vehicles.
His source of income was only selling vegetables.
There was no documentary evidence about income.
It was in the said circumstances, the claims tribunal arrived at fixing Rs.7,000/- per month as income of the deceased.
Thus, there was appropriate appreciation of facts and circumstances by the tribunal.
Point was concluded by the claims tribunal by affording sufficient reasons.
In such circumstances, there is no warrant to interfere and substitute that notional income with a different amount by this court.

In fact, the ruling that is cited at the bar is to the effect that even in those cases where the proclaimed income of an individual itself fell in dispute, the tribunals were advised to consider more appropriate amount as the income of the individual.
In such circumstances one cannot say that the approach of the claims tribunal is against law.

Therefore, the tribunal fixing Rs.7,000/- as the income of the self-employed deceased is regarded as right on facts and law Dr.
VRKS, J warranting no interference.
The rest of the calculations made by the claims tribunal and the apportions made by it and the interest awarded by it are not disputed here.
Therefore, there is no reason to disturb the impugned award here.
Point is answered against the appellant.
13. In the result, this appeal is dismissed.

Consequently, award dated 22.12.2021 of learned Chairman, Motor Vehicles Claims Tribunal - cum - Principal District Judge, Rajamahendravaram in M.V.O.P.No.481 of 2018 stands confirmed in all respects.
